newsitem.title: UK: Investors urged to oppose Airtours accounts.
newsitem.headline: Investors urged to oppose Airtours accounts.

text.p: Shareholders in UK holiday company Airtours Plc were urged on Monday to vote against the company's report and accounts when it holds its annual general meeting on Thursday.
The advice was issued by Pensions & Investment Research Consultants (PIRC) which said the company failed to comply with the Greenbury Code on corporate governance in a number of important respects.
Lobby group PIRC said that a new Long Term Incentive Plan for executives had not been put to shareholders for approval.

It is also unhappy that the executive chairman also heads the remuneration committee and that some executives have contracts with termination payments of longer than one year and the special circumstances set out by Greenbury do not apply.

"Owing to these shortcomings we consider that shareholders should register their concern by voting against the Report and Accounts," PIRC said in a report issued before Thursday's Airtours AGM in Manchester.
PIRC wants Airtours to put the incentive scheme to the vote at a future AGM.
PIRC also called on shareholders to oppose the re-election of Micky Arison, Howard Frank and Eric Sanderson as non-executive directors.

It said that Arison and Frank were not independent as they represent Carnival Corp, which has a stake of almost 30 percent in Airtours. Sanderson is chief executive of British Linen Bank Group Limited, a financial adviser to the company.
"PIRC recommends that additional independent non-executive directors be appointed to the board," the group said.
Airtours pre-tax profit in its 1996 financial year rose by 46 percent to 86.8 million pounds.
